Do the following using the steps provided in their respective sections.
        Steps:
        1. clone the repo git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
        2. analyse the contents of the repo and create following.
            2.1 create/update dockerfile based on the analysis. 
            2.2 kubernetes yamls based on the analysis.
            2.3 github actions file to build application on pushing to main branch.
        3. add all changed file to git changes 
        4. commit / push to repo

function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run recipe** that you can copy into a terminal (or paste into a shell script) and run on your own machine. It does everything you asked for: | Step | What it does | Command(s) | |------|--------------|------------| | 1 | Clone the repo | `git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git` | | 2 | Analyse the repo & generate artefacts | *See the “Analysis” section below* | | 3 | Add the new/updated files to the index | `git add Dockerfile k8s/*.yaml .github/workflows/build.yml` | | 4 | Commit & push | `git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, K8s manifests & CI workflow"`
`git push origin main` | > **NOTE** – The commands assume you have SSH access to GitHub (`git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git`) and that you’re already authenticated (e.g. via an SSH key). If you’re using HTTPS, replace the clone URL accordingly. --- ## 1. Clone the repository ```bash # 1.1 Create a working directory (optional) mkdir ~/projects && cd ~/projects # 1.2 Clone the repo git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git cd nodejs-welcome ``` --- ## 2. Analyse the repo & generate artefacts ### 2.1 Repository snapshot (what we see) > *Because I can’t actually clone the repo from here, I’ll describe the typical layout of a minimal Node.js “Hello World” project. If your repo differs, adjust the files below accordingly.* ``` nodejs-welcome/ ├─ package.json # npm dependencies + scripts ├─ src/ │ └─ index.js # main entry point ├─ .gitignore └─ README.md ``` ### 2.2 Create / update the Dockerfile Create a file named `Dockerfile` in the root of the repo with the following content: ```dockerfile # 2.2.1 Use the official Node.js slim image FROM node:18-alpine # 2.2.2 Set the working directory inside the container WORKDIR /app # 2.2.3 Copy package.json & package-lock.json first to leverage Docker cache COPY package*.json ./ # 2.2.4 Install production dependencies RUN npm ci --only=production # 2.2.5 Copy the rest of the source code COPY . . # 2.2.6 Expose the port the app listens on (adjust if your app uses a different port) EXPOSE 3000 # 2.2.7 Default command to start the app CMD ["npm", "start"] ``` > **Why this Dockerfile?** > * `node:18-alpine` is small, secure, and contains the latest LTS Node.js. > * We copy `package*.json` first so Docker can cache the `npm ci` layer. > * `npm ci --only=production` installs only the dependencies needed for runtime. > * The app is started with `npm start`, which should be defined in `package.json`. ### 2.3 Create Kubernetes manifests Create a directory `k8s/` in the repo root and add two files: `deployment.yaml` and `service.yaml`. #### 2.3.1 `k8s/deployment.yaml` ```yaml apiVersion: apps/v1 kind: Deployment metadata: name: nodejs-welcome-deployment spec: replicas: 2 selector: matchLabels: app: nodejs-welcome template: metadata: labels: app: nodejs-welcome spec: containers: - name: nodejs-welcome image: /nodejs-welcome:latest # Replace with your registry ports: - containerPort: 3000 env: - name: NODE_ENV value: production ``` #### 2.3.2 `k8s/service.yaml` ```yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: Service metadata: name: nodejs-welcome-service spec: type: LoadBalancer # Change to NodePort or ClusterIP if you prefer selector: app: nodejs-welcome ports: - protocol: TCP port: 80 targetPort: 3000 ``` > **What to change?** > * Replace `/nodejs-welcome:latest` with the actual image name you’ll push to (e.g. `ghcr.io/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest`). > * Adjust the `replicas` count or `service.type` as needed. ### 2.4 Create GitHub Actions workflow Create a directory `.github/workflows/` (if it doesn’t exist) and add a file `build.yml`: ```yaml name: Build & Push Docker Image on: push: branches: - main jobs: build: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - name: Checkout source uses: actions/checkout@v4 - name: Set up Docker Buildx uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3 - name: Log in to GitHub Container Registry uses: docker/login-action@v3 with: registry: ghcr.io username: ${{ github.actor }} password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} - name: Build and push Docker image uses: docker/build-push-action@v5 with: context: . file: Dockerfile push: true tags: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}:latest ``` > **Why this workflow?** > * It triggers on pushes to `main`. > * It builds the Docker image using the Dockerfile we created. > * It pushes the image to GitHub Container Registry (`ghcr.io`). > * It uses the built‑in `GITHUB_TOKEN` for authentication (no extra secrets required). --- ## 3. Add the new files to Git ```bash git add Dockerfile k8s/*.yaml .github/workflows/build.yml ``` --- ## 4. Commit & push ```bash git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, K8s manifests & CI workflow" git push origin main ``` > After pushing, the GitHub Actions workflow will automatically run, build the image, and push it to `ghcr.io/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest`. > You can then deploy the app to a cluster using `kubectl apply -f k8s/`. --- ### Quick sanity check ```bash # Verify Dockerfile builds locally (optional) docker build -t nodejs-welcome:local . # Run the container locally to make sure it works docker run -p 3000:3000 nodejs-welcome:local ``` If the app responds on `http://localhost:3000`, you’re good to go! --- ### Recap of what you now have | File | Purpose | |------|---------| | `Dockerfile` | Builds a lightweight Node.js image | | `k8s/deployment.yaml` | Deploys 2 replicas of the app | | `k8s/service.yaml` | Exposes the app via a LoadBalancer | | `.github/workflows/build.yml` | CI pipeline that builds & pushes the image | Feel free to tweak the replica count, service type, or image registry to fit your environment. Happy coding!
